- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–2%.
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, price often rises 1–2 days later; anticipate 1–2-day delay.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” or “reversal after peak”, model often fails to recognize it — add a 1–2 day buffer for correction.
